The retrieved context doesn't say safe mode was added in 0.125.0. The 0.125.0 changelog excerpts don't mention it. The docs do describe what the option does:

"Reject inline JavaScript assertions and shared transforms." [promptfoo/site/docs/usage/command-line.md]

More specifically:

"Use `promptfoo eval --safe-mode` or `PROMPTFOO_SAFE_MODE=true` to reject string-based JavaScript assertions and inline expressions handled by the shared transform helper." [promptfoo/site/docs/configuration/expected-outputs/javascript.md]

So it turns off inline (string-based) JavaScript assertions and inline transform expressions. You can move them into reviewed `file://` scripts instead. JavaScript function values passed through the Node API stay supported. Rejected assertions fail with an explanatory reason, and rejected transforms produce an error.

It is a limited guard, not a sandbox:

"This option is not a sandbox and does not make untrusted configurations safe to run." [promptfoo/site/docs/configuration/expected-outputs/javascript.md]

File callbacks, programmatic functions, executable providers, and config modules are not blocked (the excerpt cuts off after that list).

You can also enable it with `commandLineOptions.safeMode: true` in the config. Config settings cannot disable a guard enabled by the CLI flag or environment.
